title: Build the terminal viewer
lead: `pit view replay.jsonl`: a terminal view in `internal/tui` of memory ownership and execution pointers, driven by a replay file, with step, play, pause and seek, using ANSI escapes and the Go standard library only.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** live simulation; the web viewer.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Goal 6 and acceptance criterion C19. C31 puts the terminal viewer first because debugging needs it. This slice also creates the shared viewer fixture that the web viewer (S15) must match.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/tui/model.go`: pure frame model (cell owner per address, execution pointers per bot, cycle) built from `internal/replay`.
- `internal/tui/player.go`: the step, play, pause and seek state machine.
- `internal/tui/render.go`: ANSI renderer writing to an `io.Writer`.
- `internal/tui/model_test.go`, `player_test.go`, `render_test.go`.
- `testdata/viewer/fixture.jsonl`: a small replay (small core, few cycles) written by `pit run`, hand-checked.
- `testdata/viewer/frames.json`: the expected frame model at sampled cycles, hand-checked; S15 reuses both files.
- `cmd/pit/view.go`: the `view` subcommand; `cmd/pit/view_test.go`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestFrames`: the frame model of `testdata/viewer/fixture.jsonl` at each sampled cycle equals `testdata/viewer/frames.json`.
- `TestSeekEqualsStep`: seeking to cycle N gives the same frame as stepping N times, for every N in the fixture.
- `TestPlayer`: table-driven transitions of the step, play, pause and seek state machine, including seek past the end and before 0.
- `TestRender`: rendering a fixed frame to a `bytes.Buffer` equals a golden string in `internal/tui/testdata/`.
- `TestViewCommand` (`cmd/pit`): input commands from a `strings.Reader` drive the player and the command exits 0 at end of input.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- Standard library only: ANSI escape sequences for drawing.
- Input: Go's standard library has no portable raw-terminal mode, and golang.org/x/term would be a dependency (C13). v1 reads line-mode commands from stdin (for example `s` step, `p` play/pause, `g N` seek, `q` quit, each followed by Enter); the exact keys are the implementer's call, recorded per C35. Raw single-key input is a later change that needs owner approval of a dependency.
- Layout: a default core of 8000 cells does not fit one screen. The implementer decides the layout (for example one character per cell in fixed-width rows with paging, or downsampled blocks) and records it per C35.
- The frame model is the source of truth for C19; keep it independent of the renderer.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `. scripts/env.sh && go test ./... && go vet ./... && test -z "$(gofmt -l cmd internal)"` passes.
- Manual: `. scripts/env.sh && go run ./cmd/pit view internal/replay/testdata/imp_dwarf_seed1.jsonl`; step, play, pause and seek work in a terminal.
- The reviewer checks each C35 decision recorded by this slice.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Branch `slice/<id>-tui` in `.worktrees/<id>`. One commit when the owner asks.
